item.title: 25 Years After the Anthrax Attacks, Reauthorize and Modernize PAHPA to Better Protect Americans
item.description: Today, 25 years after the 2001 anthrax attacks, the biological threat landscape is becoming even riskier. It’s time for Congress to reauthorize and modernize the Pandemic and All Hazards Preparedness Act (PAHPA).

item.title: Space Superiority and the Military Tools to Secure It
item.description: Space superiority requires credible military options to protect U.S. forces and counter adversaries’ use of space. Integrating space control capabilities into joint operations can strengthen deterrence and preserve U.S. advantage.

item.title: Avoiding Another Long War in Yemen
item.description: In the wake of the Riyadh airport attacks, Saudi Arabia risks getting sucked into another long, costly war that ultimately only emboldens the Houthis and deepens the regional conflict. Allison Minor outlines a better approach.

item.title: Rethinking the Legal Profession’s Role in Business and Human Rights
item.description: With a key U.S. court path to corporate accountability closed and no federal due diligence mandate, lawyers are among the last safeguards for human rights. CSIS experts outline how counsel, bar associations, and courts can use existing professional rules to guard against rights harms and silencing tactics.

item.title: Cambodia’s Scam Center Cleanup: Is It Working?
item.description: In the aftermath of 2025 Thailand-Cambodia border skirmishes, scam center operations in Cambodia has captured international attention. Cambodia has implemented new legislation, sweeping crackdowns, and international anti-scam coalition building. Are these efforts working?

item.title: “Bunker Busters”: Deep Targets, Shallow Stocks
item.description: Bunker buster munitions were once a niche capability required for a small set of special targets. They have now moved into the mainstream as U.S. adversaries have responded to U.S. precision attack munitions by hardening and burying many activities.

item.title: Could Russia Be Poised to Use an On-Orbit Weapon Against a Commercial Satellite?
item.description: Cosmos 2612 is moving into position for close-proximity operations with a U.S.-registered commercial satellite supporting Ukraine. With a history of on orbit weapons tests and gray zone aggression, Russia may be betting the West won’t respond forcefully to an attack. The West must be ready to.

item.title: The Future of U.S.-UK Defense Cooperation with UK Secretary of Defence Wes Streeting
item.description: CSIS Europe, Russia, and Eurasia Program hosted a conversation with UK Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting on how both countries can keep deterrence credible in Europe and beyond.
